messages:
sam: following up on the RFC review 52 proposing a provisional-commit model for streaming at the edge. edge streams bytes to clients immediately but marks the call committed only after an upstream durability checkpoint or timeout. aim: reduce head-of-line stalls for long generations while preserving a bounded resume path. quick thoughts?
maya: sounds promising. do we change client API or keep it internal between edge and upstream?
sam: keep client API unchanged. only edge <-> upstream handshake carries commit tokens and resume metadata. client only sees a resume token if edge couldn't confirm commit before returning final state.
alex: biggest risk is duplicate side-effects from retries or re-streams. need strong idempotency for side-effectful ops or a quarantine mechanism for frames that trigger hooks.
jonah: memory/IO concerns: holding uncommitted bytes can blow memory during spikes. propose per-tenant soft caps, spill-to-disk for overflow, and a global eviction policy. set a TTL for uncommitted state (e.g., 5m).
ruth: SLO split: keep stream-visible (first-byte) latency low, but allow commit-complete latency to be higher. expose both metrics and let customers opt-in to strict commit per request via a header. default = best-effort commit.
lee: protocol sketch: client -> edge: POST /gen (idempotency_key) edge -> up: start_stream(idempotency_key, offset=0) up -> edge: stream_chunk(offset=0..k, provisional=true) edge -> client: stream_chunk(...) up -> edge: checkpoint(offset=k, commit_token=ctok) edge marks durable up to k; if final chunk and durable -> client final OK if checkpoint missing after timeout -> edge issues resume_token(rt) to client and returns partial-complete. Clients either reconnect with resume_token or accept partial result.
maya: interactive flows that rely on side-effects mid-stream need a way to declare stable checkpoints earlier. maybe upstream can emit stable-checkpoint markers the moment a side-effect is durable.
alex: testing plan: synthetic hooks record side-effect IDs, then we replay resume scenarios and assert idempotency. run chaos where checkpoint acks are dropped.
jonah: infra plan: LRU-backed spill to SSD for uncommitted bytes, add metrics: per-tenant uncommitted_bytes, spill_count, time_to_commit. enforce max_uncommitted_bytes_per_tenant and max_total_uncommitted_bytes; on eviction respond with clear error.
ruth: gating KPIs: resume_success_rate >= 99.5%, duplicate_side_effects == 0 (synthetic), no regression in stream-visible p99, and median commit latency acceptable. I'll add dashboards and alerts.
sam: suggested config knobs: soft_commit.enabled, checkpoint_timeout_ms, max_uncommitted_bytes_per_tenant, spill_to_disk_threshold, resume_window_secs, require_strict_commit_header. propose defaults: enabled=true, checkpoint_timeout_ms=12000, max_uncommitted_bytes_per_tenant=64MB, spill_to_disk_threshold=8MB, resume_window_secs=300, require_strict_commit_header=false.
lee: rollout: slow canary (5%) -> 25% -> 50%, with an A/B group that keeps behavior off. run duplicate-side-effect fuzz tests during each phase and chaotic checkpoint loss tests. tracing must correlate resume_token + commit_token + trace_id for debugging. add admin debug page (RBAC) to inspect uncommitted streams.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: edge/provisional-commit-v1 -> 5% on prod-canary cluster, monitoring 48h. logs to infra-telemetry.
alex: final note: ensure we document semantics: "partial-complete" responses must be considered non-durable unless client resumes. update SDK docs and add client examples for resuming.
sam: thanks all 52 I'll draft a short design note today. action items: alex -> duplication tests; jonah -> spill + caps; ruth -> dashboards + gating; lee -> proto sketch + upstream changes. I'll post the draft to /architecture-docs when ready.
